title: First Ramstein meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group
body:
On 26 April 2022 the United States, led by Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin, hosted a meeting at Ramstein Air Base in Germany to coordinate military support for Ukraine. It was the first meeting of what became the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, informally known as the Ramstein format. More than 40 nations attended, including NATO and EU members and countries from Africa and Asia. Japan and South Korea joined virtually.

Ukraine's Defence Minister Oleksii Reznikov attended, and the U.S. delegation included General Mark Milley. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg was expected but did not attend because of a cold, and NATO was represented by Assistant Secretary General Thomas Goffus. Austin said the group should leave with "a common and transparent understanding" of Ukraine's near-term security needs.

At the meeting Germany announced that Gepard self-propelled anti-aircraft guns would be offered to Ukraine from industry stocks and that Ukrainian soldiers would be trained on them in Germany. Germany, Canada and other nations also announced new shipments of heavy weapons. The group was to meet monthly as a contact group focused on Ukraine's self-defence and open to any country willing to contribute.
